title: A Credit-Terms Denial and an Upgraded Rating
scenario_text:
A revenue operations analyst at Jedburgh Analytics must decide whether to extend Net-60 payment terms to a customer, given how the same customer was handled earlier this year.

**Decision A (2024-02)**
Customer 'Wexford Trading' requested Net-60 terms. DENIED. Note: 'Net-60 requires a third-party credit rating of tier B or better. Wexford's rating at the time was tier D. Denied for insufficient credit rating.'

**Current request C (2024-09-08)**
Wexford Trading requests Net-60 again for a renewing contract. Since February, Wexford has posted two consecutive audited profitable quarters, and its third-party credit rating has been UPGRADED to tier B. The updated rating report is attached to the request.

**Credit Terms Policy (current, unchanged since 2023-06)**
Standard terms are Net-30. Net-60 may be extended to any customer holding a current third-party credit rating of tier B or better, verified at the time of the request. There is no other gate on Net-60. This rating requirement has been in place since June 2023.

**Slack — #revops**
AE: 'We already denied Wexford Net-60 back in February — same customer, same ask. Consistency says we deny it again.'
Analyst: 'The February denial was about their credit rating at that time. Let me check their current rating before we assume it's a repeat.'

The AE is treating the February denial as a standing decision about this customer. No one has yet re-checked Wexford's current, upgraded rating against the tier-B gate.
question: How should the analyst handle Wexford Trading's renewed Net-60 request?
choices: Deny Net-60 again, consistent with the February denial for the same customer and the same request.
Approve Net-60, because the policy is unchanged and Wexford now holds a current tier-B rating verified at request time — the February denial reflected an outdated rating that has since been upgraded.
Escalate the request to the CFO, since the customer was previously denied and the situation is sensitive.
Offer Net-45 as a compromise, given that Wexford was denied Net-60 earlier in the year.
